newsitem.title: UK: UK's Powergen in Hungarian power deal.
newsitem.headline: UK's Powergen in Hungarian power deal.

text.p: British generator Powergen Plc said on Monday it has secured a long-term power purchase agreement in Hungary, paving the way for the development of a 160 million pound ($261 million) power plant in Budapest.

Powergen, the first foreign investor to secure such an agreement in Hungary, said in a statement that its subsidiary Csepel Aramtermelo Rt had signed a 20-year contract with Hungarian state electricity supply utility MVM.

The 385 megawatt Csepel II power station is to be built on an island in the River Danube in the southern outskirts of the Hungarian capital, next to the existing Csepel station already owned by Powergen.
The new combined cycle gas turbine station is scheduled to come on stream in 2000 and supply electricity to the Hungarian national grid.

"This deal secures our third major overseas project within a month and confirms Powergen's position as one of the world's leading IPP (independent power project) developers," said group managing director Deryk King.
Powergen last month secured interests in two planned plants in Indonesia and Thailand with total generating capacity of some 1,850 megawatts.
King said that around 3,800 megawatts of new energy capacity is expected to be required in Hungary by 2010. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
